competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

central_bank_research.headline: RBA Governor Bullock: upside inflation risks materialising; housing softening
central_bank_research.summary: In her 18 September House Economics Committee opening statement, Bullock said inflation remains too high, upside risks flagged in August appear to be materialising (oil, pass-through, capacity pressures), housing has softened with prices down in most capitals, and the Monetary Policy Board meets in just over a week to assess whether tightening to date is sufficient.

central_bank_research.headline: CORRA unchanged at 2.29% through 17 September
central_bank_research.summary: Bank of Canada’s published CORRA table shows 2.29% on 15–17 September 2026 with standard publication status; compounded index updated through 18 September but no new overnight CORRA rate row beyond 17 September was shown at access time.

central_bank_research.headline: NY Fed SOFR authority unchanged at post-FOMC 3.85%
central_bank_research.institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
central_bank_research.summary: Official NY Fed secured-rates data confirm SOFR jumped to 3.85% on 17 September following the 16 September FOMC implementation window; no subsequent daily SOFR entries were available in the API snapshot taken after the freeze.

central_bank_research.headline: FOMC September SEP: median funds rate 4.1% at end-2026
central_bank_research.summary: Federal Reserve September 2026 projection materials show median participant appropriate federal funds rate at 4.1% for end-2026 and 2027, with 2026 total PCE inflation median 3.7%—supporting the SR3 strip’s further tightening pricing cited in the freeze.

news.headline: BoJ raises policy rate to 1.25% in 7–2 vote with two dissents
news.summary: Reuters reported the Board raised the policy rate 25bp to 1.25% on 18 September, with Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissenting. Commentary framed the split as reducing confidence in a rapid tightening path.

news.headline: Dollar gains vs yen after BoJ dissent; Japan reportedly conducts FX rate checks
news.summary: Reuters’ 18 September New York session piece said USD/JPY rose after the 7–2 BoJ decision and that gains partly faded after Nikkei reports of Japanese authorities conducting FX rate checks.

news.headline: Oil falls on hopes of limited Middle East supply disruption
news.summary: Reuters on 18 September reported Brent and WTI down about 1% as markets weighed alternate export routes and Saudi–Houthi strikes, extending a multi-session pullback while benchmarks remained above $100.

news.headline: Oil rises after Houthi attack on Riyadh as Asia week opens
news.summary: Reuters (21 September dateline, Singapore) said crude prices rose after 19 September Houthi missile/drone strikes on Riyadh escalated Middle East tension; treat subsequent intraday prints as unverified.

news.headline: US Leading Economic Index fell 0.1% in August
news.summary: The Conference Board’s 18 September release put the LEI at 99.5 (2016=100), with six-month growth turning slightly negative (-0.1%). Four of ten components declined; weaker consumer expectations were highlighted. Coincident index rose 0.1%.

news.headline: US initial jobless claims drop to 196,000
news.summary: Labor Department data released 17 September: seasonally adjusted initial claims fell 10,000 to 196,000 for the week ended 12 September, below consensus near 208,000; reporters cautioned Labor Day distortion. Continuing claims fell to about 1.73 million for the week ended 5 September.

news.headline: Canada Q2 job vacancies steady at 510,200
news.summary: Statistics Canada’s 15 September JVWS release showed Q2 2026 vacancies little changed at 510,200 (vacancy rate 2.8%). Total labour demand rose 0.3% q/q on higher payroll employment; offered wage growth slowed to 2.0% y/y.

news.headline: No new official SOFR fixing after 17 September 3.85% print
news.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
news.summary: NY Fed secured-rates API lists SOFR 3.85% effective 2026-09-17 as the latest entry; no 18–20 September fixings were published in that feed at research time. Weekend funding accrual still references 17 September.

research_supplement.summary: Versus the 01:50 ET freeze, the overnight increment is modest but not empty. Official funding data still anchor on the post-FOMC step-up: the NY Fed’s API shows no SOFR fixing after the 17 September 3.85% print (freeze already had that level), and Bank of Canada CORRA remained 2.29% through 17 September. The largest fresh policy signal missing from the frozen news digest is RBA Governor Bullock’s 18 September parliamentary testimony, which reiterated upside inflation risks, softer housing, and an October board meeting in just over a week. In G10 FX and rates, Friday’s BoJ 7–2 hike to 1.25% with dissents from Asada and Sato drove yen weakness and intervention-watch headlines, reinforcing the post-Fed USD/JPY bid already in the freeze’s market snapshot. US data added a mixed growth/labor read: August Conference Board LEI fell 0.1% (released 18 September) while initial jobless claims fell to 196,000 for the week ended 12 September (17 September release, holiday-distorted). Energy remains a tail for CAD/AUD inflation themes: Reuters flagged a third/fourth session of oil weakness on 18 September on alternate export-route hopes, then early 21 September Asia headlines on Houthi strikes on Riyadh. No verified post-freeze G10 FX fixing pack was found beyond the frozen 18 September marks.
